NextItNet uses causal dilated convolutions with residual connections. For stride-one layers, the derived receptive-field span is R = 1 + Σℓ(kℓ−1)dℓ. Count actual convolutions, not blocks: two width-k convolutions sharing dilation d contribute 2(k−1)d; RecBole’s NextItNet block instead uses d and 2d, contributing 3(k−1)d. Thus k=3 and block dilations [1,2,4,8] give R=61 for equal-dilation pairs, versus R=91 for d/2d pairs. Repeated stacks add their contributions. These formulas follow from the [NextItNet paper](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf) and [RecBole implementation](https://recbole.io/docs/v1.1.1/_modules/recbole/model/sequential_recommender/nextitnet.html).

RecBole explicitly pads each convolution on the left by (k−1)d, preserving sequence length and preventing access to future positions; its block applies channel LayerNorm and ReLU after each convolution, then adds the residual. Causal padding and padding-token masking are separate concerns: convolution biases and normalization offsets can make padded positions nonzero, so zero item embeddings alone do not guarantee zero intermediate padding states. Verify the supplied baseline’s masking and normalization axes; normalization across time could invalidate the purely convolutional context calculation. [Implementation source](https://recbole.io/docs/v1.1.1/_modules/recbole/model/sequential_recommender/nextitnet.html).

Implication: suffix cropping below R can remove accessible history; suffix lengths both at least R should preserve the final feature under otherwise identical, positionwise operations. For left-padded histories, read the final nonpadding position—normally index L−1—not nonpadding_count−1. The supplied baseline was not inspected, so its actual dilation schedule, receptive field, masking, and readout remain unverified.
